NFL news, live updates: Colts release Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson Sr. to start at QB; Puka Nacua potentially out for season after knee surgery

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We are officially halfway done with the 2026 NFL season, and the NFL is now into Week 11, highlighted by the year's final international game: the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Mexico, for "Sunday Night Football.".
  • Industry observers note that the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans opened up the week on "Thursday Night Football," but quarterback Daniel Jones continued to struggle, completing just 44.4% of pass attempts for 144 yards and a pick.
  • Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua might be done for the year after undergoing surgery on his MCL on Tuesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We are officially halfway done with the 2026 NFL season, and the NFL is now into Week 11, highlighted by the year's final international game: the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Mexico, for "Sunday Night Football.".

Industry observers note that the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans opened up the week on "Thursday Night Football," but quarterback Daniel Jones continued to struggle, completing just 44.4% of pass attempts for 144 yards and a pick. The Colts followed up with a statement move on Friday, announcing the team would release Jones and promote former No. 4 overall pick Anthony Richardson Sr. to the starting position in a stunning move.

Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua might be done for the year after undergoing surgery on his MCL on Tuesday. Nacua was already on injured reserve with multiple injuries, but head coach Sean McVay says that he is now poised to miss "a couple months.".

That news came one day after Nacua was reportedly suspended three games by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy, as a result of the receiver's series of incidents this offseason; Nacua is serving the suspension while on IR.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates, and more.

Industry observers note that rams running back Kyren Williams is dealing with toe soreness. Even so, head coach Sean McVay said on Saturday that Williams is still expected to play next week against the Packers.

It sounds like the bye has come at a good time for the running back.

It has been revealed that williams has played in all 10 games. He has run for 616 yards with six touchdowns on 139 carries. He also has 267 yards and a touchdown on 38 receptions.

The Detroit Lions placed center Cade Mays on injured reserve for the second time this season on Saturday.

Mays has missed Detroit's past two games since sustaining an ankle injury in Week 8's win over the Minnesota Vikings. He was also sidelined for the Lions' first five games this season with a wrist injury suffered during training camp that resulted in his first IR stint.

Going on IR means Mays will be out for the next four games. If he can return when eligible, the Lions will have four games remaining on their regular-seson schedule.

The 49ers have waived veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks.

His tenure with San Francisco ends with 58 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.

The decision comes as the team looks to play Mike Evans on Sunday night against the Vikings.

The Commanders will take on the Bengals for this week's edition of "Monday Night Football.".

Industry observers note that jacory Croskey-Merritt has been on injured reserve due to a groin injury. He is expected to play in Monday's game, but will have to be activated off IR on Sunday in order to be eligible. Otherwise, he will have to wait another week to be activated.

Sources indicate that backup running back Rachaad White is also questionable. He was limited Friday with a heel injury and did not practice Saturday.

Panthers backup running back Jonathon Brooks will have to wait another week to get activated from injured reserve.

Brooks was listed as questionable heading into the weekend due to his groin injury, but Carolina is not going to activate him for Sunday's game against the Ravens. He has been downgraded to out for the game.

The Steelers are set to get some receiving help for Sunday's game against the Eagles.

Both Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. were expected to play in the game heading into the weekend. Wilson was activated from IR on Sunday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Pittman has yet to be activated, and ESPN's Brooke Pryor reported that the Steelers are not expected to activate Pittman for Sunday's game.

The Cardinals downgraded rookie quarterback Carson Beck to out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

Beck has been dealing with back spasms this week. That means career journeyman Josh Johnson will start.

The 40-year-old QB last played in a game last January for the Commanders. He finished that game with 131 passing yards, a touchdown, and an interception.

The Titans added backup running back Tyjae Spears to injured reserve due to a knee injury.

Sources indicate that spears will miss at least the next four games. This makes him first to be eligible to return ahead of the Titans' Week 15 game against the Colts.

Industry observers note that the backup running back has played in seven games this year and has just 94 yards on 22 carries. He has caught 16 of his 18 targets for 75 more yards in the passing game.

Without Spears, Tennessee has elevated Michael Carter for Sunday's game against Dallas.

Sources indicate that the Titans will continue to lean on Tony Pollard who has been playing really well recently. Over the last three games, Pollard has 279 yards and five touchdowns on the ground and 112 yards and another score through the air.

Merritt has been out and on injured reserve since Week 5 with a groin injury. As the Commanders prepare to face the Bengals on "Monday Night Football," head coach Dan Quinn said that the running back had a "great week" and is "certainly trending the right way" to be available to play in Week 11.

According to recent reports, harrell was in his hometown of Tampa, Florida, when the accident occurred. The Titans mentioned he remains hospitalized, that the team is gathering more information, and that they will provide an patch when appropriate.

Harrell hasn't played for Tennessee this season. He tore his ACL in the preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve.

Tennessee selected the 24-year-old in the seventh round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He finished his rookie season with 13 combined tackles. Harrell improved last season, starting two of his 17 games. He finished with 25 combined tackles, including 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble.

Industry observers note that on their bye week, the Packers resume play on Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams. Jacobs recently underwent surgery to repair his fractured right ring finger, but no definitive timetable for return was declared.

Head coach Matt LaFleur stated Saturday they don't expected the running back to play in Week 12, but he will be given the opportunity to make his case in practice this week.

Tate has not played since Week 7 as he injured his shoulder. He was limited in practice on Wendesday and Thursday before being upgraded to full on Friday — an encouraging sign for his availability on Sunday as Tennessee faces the Cowboys.

The Buccaneers quarterback is expected to play Sunday against the Lions as he deals with a thumb and foot strain.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, Mayfield's foot glitch is actually a plantar fascia injury that will lead to him wearing a special orthotic and fresh cleats in order to stabilize his foot.

Mayfield has already missed three games this season due to a dislocated right thumb.

The NFL season is always chock-full of surprises and disappointments. Despite a half-year of ranking, projecting and predicting how the year will go from fans, media and league personnel alike, the bull's-eye on the dartboard that we call a typical NFL season is nigh impossible to hit. And pulling a Luke Littler on those predictions is essentially unfathomable.

Now that we're past the halfway point in the season (enjoy those sloppy island games while you can!), I wanted to highlight a few of the most pleasant surprises, along with a few disappointments that have left us with a sour taste in our mouths a week before Thanksgiving.

Sources indicate that with apologies to units like the Vikings' defense, Chiefs' offense or others at the top of the boards, I narrowed this down to units whose expectations weren't that high, or that fell way below their projected status. So I excluded the Cowboys' defense despite the group falling short of its already reasonably low expectations.

According to recent reports, friday's move was nothing short of a stunner, if only from a financial standpoint. From a football standpoint, the Colts couldn't justify keeping him as the starter? Cutting him now, knowing what a hit they'd take? It almost feels personal at this point.

According to recent reports, colts head coach Shane Steichen clearly had enough of him Thursday night. The speculation on why Steichen hadn't gone to Anthony Richardson Sr. sooner was that the coach might have trusted Richardson even less.

Sources indicate that steichen might also be in self-preservation mode, trying to hold together a ship that was partially stripped before the trade deadline and already in rough shape before that. But assuming Steichen didn't reach his breaking point during Thursday's game, why did the Colts wait to get rid of him?

It has been revealed that and not only for nothing. It actually cost the Colts money and flexibility to release him now. It doesn't get much uglier than that.

According to recent reports, it's not been the best of seasons for the 33-year-old Dupree, who has played in seven games this season. He took no defensive snaps in Weeks 8 and 9 before being a healthy scratch in Week 10 against the Ravens.

Earlier this week, he had some pointed comments about the team's front office.

"Don't ask hard questions to us; ask hard questions to them," noted Dupree, who can be a free agent this offseason. "Ask the hard questions. Everybody pull they cameras out and go upstairs and ask questions to them. Everybody. Walk upstairs and ask them.".

In a recent development, what will factor into league decisions on whether to amend the playoff structure in the coming years, or in concert with the addition of a possible 18th game? Yahoo Sports surveyed high-ranking league sources to better understand the debates from recent annual meetings as well as the most likely factors to motivate any changes.

Sources were split on whether they wanted any shift to the structure — and how that shift should materialize if it does unfold.

One high-ranking NFC executive who favors revamping the playoff structure was skeptical anything will change in the next five to 10 years, even if the schedule expands to 18 games.

Recent findings suggest that "I think it'll take an egregious deal," the executive told Yahoo Sports. "It'll take freaking someone winning the NFC South with seven wins and somebody coming in with like 12 wins. It'll take something like that, and it'd probably take an influential owner to be on that 12-win team.".

According to recent reports, patriots receiver A.J. Brown is poised to miss significant time: The wideout is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks after suffering a hastring injury last week, per ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss.

Brown has played in just four games this season after sustaining several separate injuries. He was questionable heading into last Sunday's game with ankle and knee issues, but was able to play before suffering the hamstring injury.

The Chiefs will likely be without Kenneth Walker III again for their Week 11 game against the Cardinals, head coach Andy Reid said Friday.

According to recent reports, walker reported groin tightness last week, and the team decided to give him a rest and sit out the 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Reid said on Wednesday that the running back was "feeling better," but they did not "want to do something stupid.".

Through 10 weeks, Walker is fourth in rushing in the NFL with 872 yards and tied for fifth in the league among running backs with seven touchdowns.

Read more about Walker's injury here.

Following testing, Upcoming England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reportedly suffered a fractured right fibula in Week 10, per ESPN. Maye sustained the injury after taking a sack on the first drive of Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions.

Maye will not require surgery and there is a small chance he could be back for the Patriots late in the regular season if they are contending for an AFC playoff spot.

Read more about Maye's injury here.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 14:49 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 15 November 2026.

    Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

    Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

    As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

    Bacher, 30, essentially failed to let go of the ball at the right time, leaving his team-mates stunned.

    The player himself covered his face with his hand before retrieving the ball to get play started again.

    Sources indicate that arsenal players wheeled off in celebration, only for Comunicaciones to level things up in the game soon after. Arsenal, though, scored again, and eventually won 3-2 in the first leg of the tie.

    Industry observers note that "Están matando al fútbol"Por el "insólito" gol en contra que se hace el arquero de Comunicaciones ante Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/GLUJlcKPXK.

    Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored a bizarre own goal during his side's third-tier play-off game.

    The 30-year-old failed to release the ball from a throw and released the ball into his own net.

    Fans flooded to social media to react to the scarcely believable own goal.

    According to recent reports, one wrote on X: 'Haha, those who think it's because of betting. That's the level of Argentine football.'.

    Another posted: 'RIP Argentinian football.'.

    Sources indicate that A third shared: 'The Arsenal lot celebrating... you've got some nerve.'.

    Bacher joined the club at the start of last year, but has always played in his homeland of Argentina.

    His Comunicaciones side finished ninth in their league group of Primera B, the third tier of Argentinian football, and were taken on by an Arsenal side that came second.

    They will face off in the return leg next Saturday.

    Neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    Chatterjee stated CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    Sources indicate that "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell remarked.

Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he mentioned.

    Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    In a recent development, additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    Overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the firm if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he said. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," remarked Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release Friday.
    • The artificial intelligence firm raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.
    • According to recent reports, anthropic remarked it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release Friday.

    The artificial intelligence firm raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.

    According to recent reports, anthropic remarked it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering. It sold 980 million shares on Wednesday and its underwriters had the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares by Friday as part of the overallotment, which is commonly referred to as the "greenshoe.".

    Sources indicate that shares of the Claude maker opened trading at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, but slid throughout the day and closed at $97.17. The stock sank 12% in premarket trading on Friday during a broad tech sell-off.

    In addition to the sale of its Class A common stock, Anthropic closed a concurrent sale of its Class N common stock after a group of tech companies, including Advanced Micro Devices, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and others, agreed to participate in a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price. Anthropic mentioned Friday that aggregate gross proceeds from its IPO, including the private placement, totaled $119.5 billion, before deducting offering expenses.

    Anthropic dodged an unforgiving series of obstacles on its road to the Nasdaq on Thursday, as investors brooded over Jensen Huang's shocking ouster at Nvidia, voters' stinging rebuke of the tech during the midterms and whether rising interest rates would stymie industry plans for a multitrillion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout.

    It has been revealed that CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the organization in 2021 after he and a handful of other researchers, including his sister Daniela, quit their jobs at OpenAI, now Anthropic's chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, which have captivated the corporate world and fueled the company's historic rise.

    The siblings celebrated the IPO as a "milestone" in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, but said there's more work ahead for Anthropic.

    "For us, it's like one stop on the journey," Daniela Amodei mentioned. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same company.'".

    #85159. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1033 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • Sources indicate that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    Sources indicate that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Sources indicate that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    The high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," mentioned Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That mentioned, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, mentioned Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    Industry observers note that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she mentioned.

    The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, stated Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    Industry observers note that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    In a recent development, "It is isolated," she said. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she stated.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    It has been revealed that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    According to recent reports, "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin stated. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    According to recent reports, it's also crucial to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, said R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo stated.

    It has been revealed that "That's when spreads really widen out," he said. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Trump says he discussed Jensen Huang with Xi; Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that president Donald Trump on Friday said he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week.
    • Industry observers note that "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he remarked, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant!
    • Asked earlier Friday on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" if Huang, a close ally of Trump's, had come up in "any of your discussions with the Chinese," Bessent stated "no," without elaborating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that president Donald Trump on Friday said he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week. Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the ousted leader was not mentioned in separate talks he had with Chinese officials.

    Industry observers note that "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he remarked, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He's a brilliant man.' He is," Trump said at a White House press conference.

    Asked earlier Friday on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" if Huang, a close ally of Trump's, had come up in "any of your discussions with the Chinese," Bessent stated "no," without elaborating.

    Sources indicate that A senior Trump administration official later said that both Trump's and Bessent's remarks were correct, and that both were addressing their own conversations. The official spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss those conversations.

    Trump also reiterated that he would like to see Huang — who was replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress after resigning amid allegations of an extramarital affair with a Chinese spy — be restored as Nvidia's CEO.

    "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," Trump mentioned. "You know, we're a country of second chances, and I'd love to be able to see him. That's a very crucial company to us, and he put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies.".

    Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC earlier this week.

    Industry observers note that the president's comments came amid growing scrutiny of advanced U.S. chips, including those made by Nvidia, ending up in China either legally or by being diverted via third countries.

    Both Trump's and Bessent's remarks are potentially an indication that the Trump administration may not focus on cracking down on China's efforts to acquire advanced chips.

    It has been revealed that bessent suggested that U.S. policy allowing the sale of Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips to China remains unchanged following the talks in Shenzhen this week.

    "We've already agreed that the ... H200s are the threshold level of chips that could be sold to the Chinese, and, you know, that continues as planned," Bessent stated.

    "I wouldn't anticipate any change in the policy," he added after CNBC's Sara Eisen noted that Nvidia noted it had stopped selling H200s to China.

    Sources indicate that the administration ignoring the subject of Huang's affair with a possible Chinese spy — whose Singapore-based company Megaspeed has been accused of acting as a cutout for Beijing — contrasts with the importance Trump has placed on beating China in the race to artificial intelligence dominance. It could suggest that despite his support for the U.S. AI industry, Trump is less concerned with addressing China's ongoing efforts to acquire U.S. semiconductors.

    In a recent development, trump has also defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has come under fire from multiple directions for reportedly slow-walking export restrictions on Chinese chip sales. "I understand both sides of it," Trump remarked on Monday when he also said he's like to see Huang back as CEO.

    Bessent's appearance on CNBC came after Trump's return from a tour through Asia that saw him meet with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China.

    Industry observers note that the meeting was historic as the first time the leaders of the three countries had met without other nations' counterparts. But the trilateral summit appeared to yield few deliverables on any number of the most pressing global complications related to the countries, including the Ukraine and Iran wars or the ongoing AI race.

    Bessent told CNBC on Friday that there was a "robust discussion" between Trump and Xi on trade policy and AI.

    They "agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions," he noted, abbreviating the term "super intelligence," Trump's attempted rebrand of AI.

    In a CNBC appearance last week, Bessent lamented the "leakage" of U.S.-made AI chips to China and blamed the Commerce Department, led by Lutnick, for slow-walking export controls on suspected Chinese cutouts like Megaspeed.

    Multiple Trump administration leaders have long sought to impose export restrictions on Megaspeed, but Commerce "has the pen" and "you will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent said in that interview.

    On Friday, however, Bessent was much more tight-lipped.

    Asked if there is a dispute between him and Lutnick over how aggressively the U.S. should be pursuing Chinese export controls, Bessent remarked, "I think we're all committed to following President Trump's instructions.".

    "I think we are going to see that the ... proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed," he added. Commerce recently took steps to close one of China's paths to accessing AI processors.

    Correction: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke to CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." A previous version of this story misstated the name of the show.

    Editor's note: This story and headline have been updated following additional information provided by the Trump administration about the nature of Bessent's and Trump's meetings in China.

    #85154. Warsh wants Fed officials to talk less. Instead, they’re talking more

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1054 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Warsh wants Fed officials to talk less. Instead, they’re talking more

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that in his first six months as Federal Reserve chairman, Kevin Warsh has diligently avoided signaling where he sees monetary policy and interest rates headed.
    • Fed officials have been rushing to the microphones lately, voicing sometimes conflicting opinions on how the central bank should be handling an inflation bug that the economy can't seem to shake.
    • According to recent reports, most agree that rates should be raised — and soon.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that in his first six months as Federal Reserve chairman, Kevin Warsh has diligently avoided signaling where he sees monetary policy and interest rates headed. His colleagues have been only too happy to fill the void.

    Fed officials have been rushing to the microphones lately, voicing sometimes conflicting opinions on how the central bank should be handling an inflation bug that the economy can't seem to shake.

    According to recent reports, most agree that rates should be raised — and soon. Some are willing to hike at a measured pace as conditions play out, while others, such as Governor Christopher Waller and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, entertain the thought of more aggressive hikes in a shorter period of time.

    Largely on the sidelines in the debate is Warsh, who has expressed disdain for that sort of forward guidance and argued that it handcuffs policymakers long before they actually have to make a decision. But that hasn't stopped most of the other 18 officials who sit in on Federal Open Market Committee meetings.

    In fact, according to a Bank of America analysis, there has been more so-called Fedspeak in the past two weeks than in any similar period since the start of 2025.

    "Warsh's refusal to guide markets might be encouraging the rest of the FOMC to speak more, not less," Bank of America economist Aditya Bhave remarked in a note Thursday.

    It has been revealed that "There is always a range of views across the 19 FOMC participants. Typically, the Chair would weigh in, indicating to markets whether the hawks or doves are in ascendence," he added. "Absent this leadership, however, both sides might feel incentivized to speak more often and more forcefully.".

    The increasingly vocal debate comes at a critical time for the Fed and has myriad policy implications.

    Bhave noted "a deepening divide" on the FOMC. The Fed's decision not to increase its benchmark rate at its October meeting "increasingly looks like a mistake," and as a result "the hawks have been very vocal of late," he wrote. Leading the charge is Waller, who has raised the possibility of hiking by half a percentage point when the committee next meets in December.

    Minutes from the October meeting hint at the tension, particularly when it comes to Warsh's refusal to provide guidance.

    The summary related that some officials who were looking for a hike in October "could have supported no change in the federal funds rate provided that it was clearly understood by market participants that further tightening was likely" — a statement that points toward the forward guidance that Warsh has insisted the Fed avoid.

    The minutes "revealed that some officials favoring a hike would have accepted a hold if the Fed had clearly communicated further tightening," market veteran Ed Yardeni wrote Thursday. "Warsh's communication philosophy may thus be limiting the Fed's flexibility precisely when it needs it most.".

    Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, who voted against the October pause in favor of a quarter-point hike, tiptoed around the forward guidance problem during a recent public appearance.

    Sources indicate that prefacing some observations she made about where she sees policy headed, Hammack noted that, "Those are not promises. Those are not commitments. They're not forward guidance, which is a hot-button topic. But what they are are a conditional set of expectations of where I think the economy can go, based on what I'm seeing.".

    Hammack's comments illustrate a needle that Fed officials have been trying to thread: continuing to be transparent about their thinking without appearing locked into a future policy that changing economic conditions could render obsolete.

    Speaking Thursday, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee framed the argument around credibility.

    "I am sympathetic to the view that [Warsh] has expressed that let's not be so, in in our language, forward guidance-oriented, saying here is what I think rates are going to be at the next meeting," Goolsbee noted, calling such pronouncements "falsely precise.".

    However, he quickly separated forward guidance from transparency.

    Recent findings suggest that "I think central banks should be careful about doing anything that undermines credibility," Goolsbee noted. "That said, I also think that it's pretty important [that] each person who sits around that table explain how they see the world. What do you see in business conditions? You don't want to surprise everybody.".

    Taking a slightly different tack, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson, in a speech Thursday on policy communication, insisted that markets can figure out where policymakers are going without specific guidance so long as they understand how economic developments will influence decisions.

    Paulson also defended the variety of voices coming from the Fed.

    "But volume is not the same as clarity," she said. "The measure is not how much we say. It is whether we are understood." The mixture of voices "guards against any single communication becoming the only one that matters.".

    Financial markets have taken the plethora of Fed communications and interpreted it in a fairly hawkish way.

    Traders are implying a 100% chance of at least a quarter percentage point hike in December, with a very small probability of a half-point move, according to the CME Group's FedWatch. From there, odds are high for a follow-up increase in January, then perhaps one more before the end of 2027.

    While current inflation indicators are running above 3%, compared to the Fed's 2% target, market measures of longer-term inflation have declined.

    Sources indicate that five-year forward expectations, as indicated through the Treasury market, are at their lowest since April. That suggests investors could be less concerned about inflation over the longer term, even as policymakers warn that current price pressures remain elevated.

    Still, a sclerotic communications strategy from the Fed amid volatile economic and geopolitical currents could prove dangerous ahead.

    "The result of this back-and-forth is undue rates volatility in already turbulent times," BofA's Bhave said.

    For his part, Warsh has been advocating for a "family fight" atmosphere inside the Fed, arguing that competing viewpoints deserve a full airing as the committee works towards decisions.

    "There are benefits to shaping the market's future expectations. Perhaps this is part of the 'family fight' that Warsh keeps referencing in his pressers," stated Tom Graff, chief investment officer at advisory firm Facet. "That family fight seems to be happening out in public.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    In a recent development, health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The tech giant also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround proposal.

    Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

    According to recent reports, the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the manufacturer's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the manufacturer's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    Industry observers note that wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the manufacturer's AI strategy when it reveals its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    According to recent reports, heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Recent findings suggest that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," remarked the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the manufacturer's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    According to recent reports, morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    Next is semiconductor firm Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    Sources indicate that the five-star analyst stated that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    In a recent development, while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    Svanberg mentioned that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    It has been revealed that svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Top Wall Street analysts prefer these 3 dividend stocks for stable income

    📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade.
    • Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a organization's ability to pay dividends consistently.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a organization's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    In a recent development, integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The company has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    According to recent reports, in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the manufacturer's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Sources indicate that specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    It has been revealed that furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    It has been revealed that "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

    It has been revealed that mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream firm operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    In a recent development, ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the manufacturer to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    The 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

    Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent announced an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    Heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from new shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," noted Richardson.

    Sources indicate that the 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

    The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable tech giant, regardless of market conditions.

    • Published: 15:51 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 15:52 EST, 15 November 2026.
    • Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.
    • The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar confirmed his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 15:51 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 15:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

    Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.

    The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar confirmed his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.

    Having enjoyed retirement for 11 years, he shocked world football by agreeing a surprise transfer to Serie C outfit Ravenna, where he was set to undertake a marketing role.

    It was initially understood that he would not be making a playing return, but the Brazil legend laced up his boots on Sunday and played a part in his side's opening goal.

    Ravenna's honorary vice president Ariedo Braida remarked in June that the World Cup winner would regrettably not be able to play for the club due to his age.

    But it appears that went up in smoke, with Ronaldinho playing 45 minutes on his return in the league clash – despite his move being dubbed a publicity stunt by the club.

    Brazil icon Ronaldinho has made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46.

    He played the first-half of the game, playing a role in the first goal for his fresh side.

    He helped set up Giulio Donati's opening goal of the match, and raced across the field to mob the goal scorer as he celebrated.

    He started the game, playing the first-half before being replaced by Matteo Maggio. Before his substitution, he embraced the fans in the stands at the interval.

    The icon hinted there could be more games to come, however.

    He told Sky Italia after the game: 'It went by too fast, that has always been football for me.

    'Is this my last one? I don't know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.

    'It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.'.

    Ronaldinho has also become a shareholder in the club.

    During his illustrious career, he won the World Cup, a Champions League, two LaLiga titles and a Serie A trophy before hanging up his boots in 2015.

    He also won a string of individual accolades including the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and FIFA World Player of the Year in 2004 and 2005.

    #85118. Data center construction costs soar 13% in 2026

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (517 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Data center construction costs soar 13% in 2026

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The demand for large-scale data centers in the U.S.
    • It has been revealed that all that resulted in costs rising 13% year-over-year to more than twice the global rate, according to a new report from Turner & Townsend, a global project management tech giant.
    • It has been revealed that the report looked at over 500 live or recently completed projects in 62 global markets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The demand for large-scale data centers in the U.S. this year, driven by the need for computing power for artificial intelligence, grew well beyond the supply of powered land and the labor to build these structures. It also pushed timelines and risk for contractors.

    It has been revealed that all that resulted in costs rising 13% year-over-year to more than twice the global rate, according to a new report from Turner & Townsend, a global project management tech giant. The gain this year was about three times the last ten-year average.

    It has been revealed that the report looked at over 500 live or recently completed projects in 62 global markets. It also included a survey of 400 experts in the global data center industry.

    While there was some stabilization in cost inflation this year, it was not enough to offset the huge growth in not just demand but speed of construction and delivery.

    It has been revealed that "More aggressive schedules tie to contractors in particular and subcontractors baking in more risk allowances in their pricing," said Paul Barry, North America data center lead for Turner & Townsend. "So whether that's acceleration allowances, whether that's more overtime and labor attraction allowances, even just higher fees for taking on the risk of delivering at a faster pace than what they would traditionally take on.".

    All of those things, combined with the spike in demand and the strain on the supply chain, translate into higher costs, he added.

    Capital expenditure on global data centers is projected to rise from about $800 billion this year to $1.8 trillion per year in 2050, according to a recent report from PwC. The U.S. is expected to capture almost half of all global investment in AI infrastructure, which includes both data centers and chips.

    Power is, of course, key to all data centers, and 56% of those surveyed by Turner & Townsend globally said it was a major obstacle to delivery. Just over half said utility connections typically take between one and two years, and almost a third reported timeframes of over two years. Costs for power vary regionally — from $15.01 per watt in Silicon Valley to $10.51 per watt in Dallas, based on a typical 60-megawatt design.As with every type of construction in the U.S., labor continues to be a significant headwind. Just over one quarter of respondents said their contractor capacity, that is, the ability to manage construction backlogs, was sufficient.

    Going forward, Barry noted he expects costs to moderate somewhat, with cost increases in the 6% to 10% range in the next year. A lot of the major projects have already started or are starting now, so cost risk has been baked into those contracts.

    "If this demand continues, then there'll be more continued flow of project starts and so on, but I think we've hit a big surge in 2026, especially of new big major projects that have been procured," remarked Barry.

    According to recent reports, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    According to recent reports, robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly vital sources of transaction revenue, while the organization has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    It has been revealed that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Industry observers note that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    Tech Report: Trump vows to stop U.S. companies from building data centers abroad, threatens 'tremendous tax'

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump on Friday noted U.S.
    • "We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump said at a White House press conference before announcing the latest policy — which apparently came as news to his own staff.
    • Industry observers note that "I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump mentioned.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump on Friday noted U.S. companies will be banned from building data centers in other countries and will face a "tremendous tax" penalty if they do so.

    "We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump said at a White House press conference before announcing the latest policy — which apparently came as news to his own staff.

    Industry observers note that "I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump mentioned. "I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now they're here.".

    In a recent development, trump's latest push for more data-center construction in the U.S. came despite Americans repeatedly stating — and showing with their votes — that they dislike the structures.

    CNBC's All-America Economic Survey found that 64% of registered voters opposed an AI data center within 10 miles of their home, while just 13% of respondents said they would support one.

    In a recent development, if Trump follows through on his threat to clamp down on overseas data center construction, he will have to contend with the fact that numerous U.S. tech giants — including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle — have already built them in other countries.

    International expansion represents a growth opportunity for the top cloud infrastructure providers, which want to serve clients from data centers that are nearby, sometimes to meet regulatory requirements.

    Trump said Friday, however, that if companies want to continue building the centers outside the U.S., "they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them.".

    "We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. They have energy, and they have everything. They're tremendous assets," Trump said.

    Representatives at cloud providers Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

    Trump's remarks came a day after Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China for a trilateral summit that appeared to produce few concrete deliverables on an array of pressing global issues.

    Xi "congratulated me on how well we're doing" in artificial intelligence, Trump said, using his preferred term "super intelligence," which he said the Chinese president also likes better.

    — CNBC's Jordan Novet and Annie Palmer contributed reporting.

    The ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S. midterm elections have been keeping investors busy. Further, worries about elevated artificial intelligence spending are weighing on investor sentiment.

    Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    This week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The company will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG shows the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

    Heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

    Ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

    The five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

    "We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," said Ikeda.

    Striker Che Adams claims Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli is significant on the small details... 'he loves his FaceTime calls'

    📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (931 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
    • Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.
    • No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

    Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

    No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

    Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be massive on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

    Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the new man’s first get together in La Manga.

    ‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

    ‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

    Industry observers note that ‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

    Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli.

    Striker Adams says Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'.

    John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

    ‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

    ‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

    ‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’.

    Recent findings suggest that hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

    ‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

    ‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

    ‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

    ‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’.

    John McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

    Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

    ‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

    ‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

    ‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

    Sources indicate that ‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

    It has been revealed that ‘He said to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

    ‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

    ‘It was very important to get the win and build up the confidence.

    ‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

    ‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’.

    The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

    On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

    Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

    ‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ mentioned Adams.

    ‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

    Industry observers note that ‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

    ‘He’s not going to stop until he does.

    Industry observers note that ‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

    Industry observers note that ‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

    ‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

    ‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’.
