    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the 2026 college football season has been defined by chaos, with examples every other weekend that there’s never been more parity than ever before.
    • As Saturday’s action draws to a close and Week 12 wraps up, let’s dive into Sportsnaut’s Week 13 college football rankings.
    • South Carolina did have LaNorris Sellers back on Saturday, so this isn’t the same South Carolina team that lost 34-6 to Arkansas.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the 2026 college football season has been defined by chaos, with examples every other weekend that there’s never been more parity than ever before. Saturday proved that once again, with the undefeated UCLA Bruins losing to a five-loss Michigan team and the reigning national champion Indiana Hoosiers again losing because of missed field goals.

    As Saturday’s action draws to a close and Week 12 wraps up, let’s dive into Sportsnaut’s Week 13 college football rankings.

    South Carolina did have LaNorris Sellers back on Saturday, so this isn’t the same South Carolina team that lost 34-6 to Arkansas. With that noted, the Georgia Bulldogs actually found themselves trailing 6-2 midway in the second quarter at Williams-Brice Stadium. Georgia took the lead before the half, but the switch really seemed to be flipped in the third quarter when the Bulldogs put up two scoring drives (10 points) and their defense rounded back into form. Georgia (10-1) can now return home for its final prep before facing Georgia Tech, at least knowing it has complete control of its path to the No. 1 seed in the College Football Playoff.

    According to recent reports, with Ohio State losing again this weekend, can the national conversation about Devon Dampier being a legitimate Heisman Trophy candidate start now? He might not have the best numbers in the nation, but the senior quarterback has produced 31 total touchdowns this season and largely carried the Utah Utes to an undefeated record. Dampier has come through in massive moments, including a four-touchdown performance to win the Holy War along with 150 rushing yards and two touchdowns in a win against Houston. All we’re saying is the star quarterback of the undefeated team that’s No. 2 in the college football rankings deserves more Heisman buzz than Dampier is receiving.

    The Notre Dame Fighting Irish were never going to do to SMU what Wake Forest did, that’s just not the style of football this team plays. Saturday’s home thrashing of the Mustangs, at least by the Fighting Irish’s standard, was an impressive display of what this offense is capable of when things are clicking. With UCLA’s loss on Saturday, Notre Dame’s path to a top seed just became a bit clearer. The Fighting Irish will close out their regular season on Saturday at Syracuse.

    Recent findings suggest that seizing on the confidence built from his game-winning drive against LSU, quarterback Arch Manning came out on Saturday and lit up Arkansas early. The Texas Longhorns jumped out to a 17-3 lead, thanks to a Manning touchdown and KJ Jackson’s pick-six, setting the tone for a one-sided game in Austin. Texas (9-2) now gets ready for a trip to Kyle Field, where this Longhorns defense will have plenty of chances to exploit an abysmal Aggies offense.

    The Tennessee Volunteers have a blueprint for success and, for the most part, it keeps working. On a night when they turned it over three times, turning into 13 points for LSU, this was a 13-13 game entering the fourth quarter. After three dominant quarters from Tennessee’s defense in a physical game, the Volunteers’ unleashed true freshman Faizon Brandon’s athleticism (112 yards and 2 touchdowns) and he carried them to victory. A soul-crushing defense and a ground game that makes its opponent experience death by a thousand paper cuts, it’s not pretty football but it’s the reason Neyland Stadium will be hosting a College Football Playoff game.

    Related: Winners, Losers from Tennessee Volunteers’ 27-13 Win Over LSU.

    Sources indicate that ahead of Week 11, head coach Kalen DeBoer called this the “most complete” he’s ever had with the Alabama Crimson Tide. That might be true, though it’s worth remembering the two previous iterations of this team in the DeBoer era each lost four games. Alabama also didn’t exactly play its best football early against Chattanooga, but they did look unstoppable once the wheels were in moton. We’re not using that game as a point of evidence that the Crimson Tide’s rushing offense is back on track. Alabama (9-2) gets the Iron Bowl next, and we have more than enough faith in quarterback Keelon Russell along with Kane Wommack’s defense to think they punch a ticket to an SEC Championship Game with a rematch versus Georgia.

    Here’s the good news for the Miami Hurricanes: Mario Cristobal finally has a second win in games where his team trails by 12-plus points. Why did Miami trail 14-3 at home against Virginia Tech? A rare Darian Mensah interception and your typical work from the Hurricanes defense. As fun as Miami’s offense can be to watch, we just can’t put this team in the same tier as Tennessee, Alabama and Texas because its defense is a glaring Achilles heel and we don’t have a ton of faith in the head coach either.

    Sources indicate that stop us if you’ve heard this before. The Wake Forest Demon Deacons blew the doors off their opponent. Similar to last week’s victory at SMU, the Demon Deacons came out of the gate firing with a 36-7 lead at halftime. The game was well in hand by that point, with Wake Forest taking its foot off the brake and coasting to a win at Georgia Tech. Jake Dickert’s Demon Deacons are now 10-1 on the season and get to close things out next week at home against a Duke program that just lost to Clemson. Once that’s behind them, Wake Forest gets its rematch vs. Miami in the ACC Championship Game.

    In a recent development, margin of victory matters when stacking up the best college football teams in 2026, and needing triple overtime to beat Kansas (4-7) after missing a game-winning field goal as time expired in the fourth isn’t exactly a quality win for the BYU Cougars. Bear Bachmeier simply hasn’t been an effective passer as of late, and his continued struggles through the air on Saturday (15-of-26, 173 pass yards and 6.7 ypa) nearly cost BYU dearly with his arm in regular. It’s getting more difficult to justify putting the Cougars (9-2) in the College Football Playoff, but that win over Notre Dame paired with losses by Indiana and UCLA make earning a spot all but a guarantee.

    Taking on a Baylor team that has looked more competitive since the firing of Dave Aranda, the Texas Tech Red Raiders were still able to win by 10 points even with three turnovers and a 23.1% third-down conversion rate. Thomas Castellanos (2 interceptions) did remind everyone of his limitations as a passer, but those can be limited a bit when the team can run for over 200 yards and has its defense allow just a single touchdown on a drive that started at the Texas Tech 26-yard line. There were no style points in the victory for the Red Raiders, but those aren’t necessary on a weekend where UCLA and Indiana both lost.

    Industry observers note that the UCLA Bruins aren’t making the College Football Playoff. We’re only dropping them to 11th out of some respect for their season-long accomplishments, but head coach Bob Chesney is now forced to start third-string quarterback Madden Iamaleava next week against USC. Based on how Iamaleava looked tonight, it’s hard to imagine how the Bruins win that game unless this defense delivers its best performance of the season. This is a devastating end to an unbelievable 2026 campaign for the Bruins.

    In a recent development, rivalry games are tough, especially on the road against a six-win Illinois team with designs of snuffing out the Iowa Hawkeyes’ playoff hopes. This was a 17-17 game until late in the second quarter, when Iowa woke up and delivered 17 unanswered points to take full control of the game. Fittingly, it was the run game (263 yards, 3 touchdowns and 5.1 yards per carry) that carried the Hawkeyes to another victory. Iowa (9-2) has won four in a row and will be hoping to achieve a double-digit win season and hand Nebraska a new losing streak against ranked opponents.

    The Indiana Hoosiers avoided their second loss of the season a few weeks ago against Minnesota because Paddy McAteer made a 60-yard field goal, so we won’t come down too harshly on the young man for the missed 37-yard attempt in overtime that lost the game on Saturday. Kicking woes have been an matter for the Hoosiers this year, however, with Nico Radicic’s two missed field goals proving costly in the 19-15 loss at home to Ohio State. With the loss, the reigning national champions just opened the door to not even making the CFP this season.

    Sources indicate that what a run it’s been for quarterback Dylan Raiola. Following Friday’s performance, a 45-7 win at Michigan State, the junior sports a 10-0 TD-INT ratio with 1,168 passing yards. The Oregon Ducks are 4-0 in that stretch, with two of those being wins against ranked opponents (Northwestern and Ohio State). Dan Lanning deserves some credit for this team not giving up on the season. Although, one does wonder what would’ve happened if a change at offensive coordinator came earlier in the year. Even with the late move, Oregon now just needs a win next week and a UCLA loss to earn a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game.

    Sources indicate that barring a stunning loss, the Boise State Broncos will represent the Group of Five in the College Football Playoff. The good news for the program, assuming that happens, is that it will be the second playoff appearance under head coach Spencer Danielson. With that stated, the current state of Boise State’s defense has them ripe for getting blown out in the first round. It does bring back the debate a bit of whether it’s better to make the CFP and be destroyed in a first-round exit or appear in a good bowl game and end the season with a win.

    According to recent reports, trailing 28-20 with 2:09 left on the clock, senior quarterback Noah Fifita led the Arizona Wildcats on the last-minute comeback with a 35-yard touchdown strike to Isaiah Mizell followed by the game-tying, two-point conversion on a trick play to get this one into overtime. Fifita delivered again, this time finding Giovanni Richardson in the end zone for the go-ahead score in the first overtime. Kansas State had a chance, but a huge stop on 4th-and-1 secured the Wildcats’ eighth win of the season. It wasn’t the most impressive of victories, but this is still an 8-3 team that has only lost to BYU, Texas Tech and Utah.

    The USC Trojans trailed 14-13 at home heading into halftime Saturday against Maryland (4-7). Thankfully for Lincoln Riley, a missed field goal seemed to throw the Terrapins out of whack as they went three-and-out or were intercepted on each of their next four drives to turn a one-point lead into a 21-point deficit in the fourth quarter. Although, it probably doesn’t make the Trojans feel great that their “quality loss” to Indiana looks a lot worse a week later given the Hoosiers just got taken out by the Huskies.

    Recent findings suggest that considering how the College Football Playoff committee treated South Carolina for losing with a backup quarterback, maybe the Houston Cougars wouldn’t have been dropped from the Top 25 if they lost Saturday with Conner Weigman sidelined. We’ll never know. The fan base got a preview of the future, with true freshman quarterback Keisean Henderson making his first start. He wasn’t flawless, though he responded to a 10-point deficit late in the third quarter with three consecutive scoring drives, including the game-winning drive. Houston (8-3) now gets to close out its regular season against Baylor, with there being a strong likelihood of history repeating itself for the second consecutive year with the ninth win of the year coming against the Bears.

    It has been revealed that the Louisville Cardinals couldn’t get anything going on the ground Saturday night versus Pittsburgh. Fortunately, the gap at quarterback between Lincoln Kienholz and Holden Geriner made the difference in this game. Whereas the Panthers’ quarterback was picked off twice and averaged just 4 yards per attempt, Kienholz carried the Cardinals’ offense with four total touchdowns in the first three quarters. Given a 14-point lead, Louisville’s defense feasted on a Pitt passing game that still couldn’t get anything going with Corey Dailey under center. Louisville rides a six-game win streak into Kentucky for the regular-season finale.

    Sources indicate that what a difference it makes to have a competent offensive coordinator who puts the players he has in position to succeed. The Oklahoma Sooners put up 28 unanswered points on Saturday night in their 21-point victory over Texas A&M, pushing this forward to a three-game win streak and two of those were by a touchdown-plus against ranked SEC teams. We’re not saying Oklahoma belongs in the playoff, but the version of this team we’ve seen in November has been a top-20 program in college football.

    The Florida Gators seem to hate making the Top 25 college football rankings. Aaron Philo did pull out the victory on Saturday in The Swamp, though it was aided by Vanderbilt (4-7) wide receiver Junior Sherrill making an uncharacteristic drop that might’ve been a conversion on third-and-21 to set the Commodores up inside the red zone with 30 seconds left. Instead, Florida (7-4) survived. It means they get to remain a Top 25 team, which might spell trouble ahead of the regular-season finale against Florida State.

    It has been revealed that nothing can be taken from a blowout win at home against Wofford. Trinidad Chambliss put up fantastic numbers (19-of-20, 367 passing yards and 5 touchdowns), though it’s his struggles against ranked teams (59.2% completion rate, 11-7 TD-INT and 6.9 ypa) that helped derail the Ole Miss Rebels’ season after that 5-1 start. Mississippi should not have much trouble closing out the regular season with a win at home in the Egg Bowl, though an 8-4 record without a playoff appearance is a tough finish considering the level of expectations reached after the Sept. 19 win against LSU.

    Eli Drinkwitz’s Missouri Tigers beat a ranked team, how about that. Outside of one mistake (interception), Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons was nearly flawless (16-of-21, 300 yards and four touchdowns) in three quarters of dominance against the Wildcats defense. When he’s playing at that level, you don’t need Jamal Roberts and Ahmad Hardy to do much. This feels like a win Missouri really needed, given it had lost four of its last five. However, that Week 13 matchup at home against Oklahoma looks far more challenging than it would have a month ago.

    Sources indicate that would the Liberty Flames (10-1) lose by 21-plus points to every team in our top 25 college football rankings in a head-to-head matchup? Absolutely. With that remarked, at some point you have to give credit to a team that has won 10 consecutive games. The Flames are absolutely taking advantage of arguably the easiest schedule in college football, and their lone loss to James Madison captures that pretty well. Still, 10 wins is 10 wins.

    Plenty of top 25 teams are getting credit nationally for still winning games with a backup quarterback. New Mexico Lobos head coach Jason Eck lost his starter Jack Layne right before the season kicked off, leaving him to rely on To’a Fa’avae (8-8 TD-INT, 58.5% completion rate and 22 sacks taken) and he still kept winning. In Saturday’s victory against Wyoming, New Mexico turned to Luke Moga and came out on top despite losing the turnover battle. It’s a 9-2 campaign for the Lobos and we can’t wait to see who comes out on top against Air Force in the battle of arguably the two best teams in the Mountain West.

    Sources indicate that the South Carolina Republican confirmed earlier this week that Huang had agreed to appear, but the details of that appearance remained unclear. Huang, who resigned from the tech giant he co-founded earlier this month over a series of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, also reached an agreement with three House committees to appear for a closed-door, transcribed interview on Dec. 1.

    According to recent reports, the date of Huang's public testimony in the Senate has not yet been announced, though Scott initially requested he appear on Dec. 3.

    President Donald Trump on Friday mentioned he has not lost confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, pushing back on growing pressure from bipartisan lawmakers and even members of his own administration.

    Trump, at a wide-ranging White House press conference, was asked about Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., telling The Wall Street Journal that, if Lutnick is to be ousted, it should happen soon enough for the Republican-led Senate to confirm his replacement before Democrats take over the chamber.

    Nvidia stock plunges 14%, wraps up longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.
    • Nvidia shares tumbled 14% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang.
    • Shares of Nvidia are down 46% over the period, pushing the organization's market cap down by about $2.6 trillion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.

    Nvidia shares tumbled 14% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang. The stock closed lower for a seventh consecutive week, the longest such stretch since 2008.

    Shares of Nvidia are down 46% over the period, pushing the organization's market cap down by about $2.6 trillion. The stock is now trading at roughly 8.4 times forward earnings, while Advanced Micro Devices is valued at 29 times profit for the next 12 months.

    On Friday, Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is exploring potential accounting problems at Nvidia, pushing the stock down further.

    Once the most valuable company in the world, Nvidia now has a market cap of $3 trillion, putting it fourth behind Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet.

    In a recent development, nvidia is reeling from the removal of Huang, who resigned on Nov. 12, after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly a spy.

    Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, said earlier this week that Huang had resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms.".

    But the chipmaker's losing streak started before Nvidia was thrown into crisis as investors worried over the sustainability of the AI buildout, particularly after the midterm elections, and emerging competition in AI chips from Google and AMD.

    Industry observers note that even a better-than-expected earnings report, which included an increase to fiscal 2028 guidance, didn't stem the selling. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the company's longtime CFO, projected revenue growth next fiscal year of 75%, and mentioned that customers aren't going anywhere.

    On Tuesday's earnings call with analysts, Kress signed off by saying, "we've got this." In a organization meeting the next day, executives told staff that it was moving its yearly review process, which can come with more stock, from March to December.

    For investors, one major question is whether Nvidia can continue to innovate and sustain its commanding lead in the AI chip market without its visionary leader. Almost the entire tech giant now is built around the AI trade, a phenomenon that began taking hold just four years ago with the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT.

    Industry observers note that before that, Nvidia's primary business was selling graphics cards used for video games. In mid-2008, the last time the stock was this deep into a weekly losing streak, Nvidia was generating less than $1 billion per quarter. Now it pulls in more than $1 billion per day. At the time, the entire market was in freefall due to the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SHENZHEN, China — For a second year in a row, Chinese President Xi Jinping has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores.
    • President Donald Trump had a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday, after the three met the prior evening during a welcome banquet for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen.
    • According to recent reports, in September 2025, Xi, Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly laughed together for a friendly photo-op alongside an annual meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Tianjin, China.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SHENZHEN, China — For a second year in a row, Chinese President Xi Jinping has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores.

    In a recent development, U.S. President Donald Trump had a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday, after the three met the prior evening during a welcome banquet for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen. It marked the first time they had met together in person.

    According to recent reports, in September 2025, Xi, Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly laughed together for a friendly photo-op alongside an annual meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Tianjin, China. The gathering followed easing tensions between Beijing and Newly introduced Delhi.

    Recent findings suggest that china's "ability to engage directly with the world major powers" reflects the country's influence across the Global South and Eurasia, said Jodie Wen, postdoctoral fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University. "China hopes to play a more constructive role in this conflict-[ridden], unstable world.".

    In the future, "China will hope to provide more platforms" within its borders for countries to discuss problems, she mentioned.

    Trump, Xi, Putin remarked they blueprint to boost oil production, revamp UN after trilateral talks.

    It has been revealed that I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways.

    Trump holds talks separately with Putin and Xi ahead of their historic trilateral meeting.

    Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019.

    Why the Middle East is watching the Trump-Xi-Putin summit.

    Trump arrives in China for historic meeting with Xi, Putin.

    China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers.

    Putin claims EU is losing industry, falling behind competition.

    Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China.

    China has increasingly played the role of broker, for instance, providing the forum for restoring diplomatic ties between Saudi Arabia and Iran in 2023.

    According to recent reports, by participating in and hosting different multilateral organizations, China has stayed in the Western orbit while cultivating relations with non-Western countries. The two photo-ops last year and this year reflect only a portion of Xi's large number of meetings with different world leaders.

    Recent findings suggest that xi has hosted more than 40 heads of state so far this year, including at least eight around the APEC meetings in Shenzhen this week. That's on top of receiving over 60 state visits in 2025, according to CNBC analysis of official Chinese readouts.

    Domestic Chinese media have highlighted how Xi has met with many foreign leaders around the China-hosted events.

    "Beijing sees these multilateral platforms as opportunities to expand its international influence and demonstrate its commitment to multilateralism, while bilateral diplomacy remains equally crucial," said Yue Su, principal economist for China at EIU.

    But she noted that different countries increasingly pursue different geopolitical and economic priorities, making it challenging to reach consensus even through multilateral organizations.

    "Against this backdrop, China's diplomatic priorities are increasingly focused on delivering tangible economic benefits through trade, investment, financial connectivity and technology cooperation," she mentioned.

    On Thursday, Xi announced at the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting that China would provide $20 million in support for the Asia Pacific region. He also advocated for the development of an "Asia-Pacific community with a shared future," an iteration of his commonly used slogan on a "shared future" for humanity more broadly.

    The Shenzhen summit can create meaningful outcomes for crisis management, as well as diplomatic space for future negotiations, Tsinghua University's Wen said. She added that it's vital for leaders to come together in person in order to avoid misunderstandings and further tensions.

    Trump remarked Thursday at the trilateral that the U.S., China and Russia are "uniquely positioned" to discuss reducing nuclear weapons at their historic meeting. A Chinese readout subsequently said the three leaders discussed Ukraine, the Middle East and the Korean Peninsula.

    —CNBC's Matthew Tan contributed to this report.

    Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting substantial moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the manufacturer that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the manufacturer's after-market report on Tuesday.

    Since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is presently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    According to recent reports, with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    Warren Buffett quadruples Thanksgiving gifts: A breakdown of how much wealth he's giving away

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1401 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Warren Buffett, 96, more than quadrupled his Thanksgiving donations to four family foundations this year to $5.5 billion.
    • The gifts consist of Berkshire Class B shares that have been converted from his roughly $160 billion of Class A shares.
    • The increase is in line with his new goal, announced last July, to give away all of his Berkshire Hathaway shares "within about eight years," with no additional annual donations going to the Gates Foundation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Warren Buffett, 96, more than quadrupled his Thanksgiving donations to four family foundations this year to $5.5 billion.

    The gifts consist of Berkshire Class B shares that have been converted from his roughly $160 billion of Class A shares.

    The increase is in line with his new goal, announced last July, to give away all of his Berkshire Hathaway shares "within about eight years," with no additional annual donations going to the Gates Foundation.

    It has been revealed that around $2.2 billion of shares goes to the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, named for his late first wife, with the three foundations run by his children, Susie Buffett's Sherwood Foundation, the Howard G. Buffett Foundation, and Peter Buffett's NoVo Foundation each getting $1.1 billion each.

    In July of last year, Buffett gave shares worth $4.6 billion to the Gates Foundation with another $1.4 billion going to the family foundations.

    This July, the family foundations received $5.9 billion in stock, bringing the year's total to $11.4 billion, an increase of almost 55% from last year, even as the Gates Foundation received nothing.

    In comments included in the Berkshire news release this week announcing the new gifts, Buffett reaffirmed his confidence in his children's ability to disburse his fortune over time, saying they "have given thoughtfully to worthy causes for decades, and I trust 100% both their abilities and their fidelity.".

    He also mentioned his confidence in Berkshire is "as strong as ever.".

    Recalling that in last year's lengthier Thanksgiving message he had mentioned, "Kindness is costless but also priceless," Buffett wrote, " A year later, I would only add that it compounds, and at a better rate than anything Charlie [Munger] and I ever bought.".

    According to recent reports, "Both of us received beyond measurement costless benefits from a few teachers such as Ben Graham, Joe Rosenfield and Tom Murphy. Because of this we not only prospered mightily but were able to pass along many of the benefits we received.

    "Much of my good fortune has come in the form of people who were kind to me and expected nothing in return. I'm grateful to every one of them.

    "This Thanksgiving, thank one of those selfless people in your own life. Better yet, be a benefactor for someone else.".

    Berkshire Hathaway's fourth quarter rally that had produced a string of record highs cooled this week as both classes of its stock posted five straight daily declines.

    That sent them down 3.9% for the week.

    Last Friday, Berkshire was up 19.1% since October 1. Now that gain has been cut to 14.5%.

    The S&P's decline of 8.6% this week, however, was even bigger than Berkshire's 5-day drop, as investors sold to lock in profits from AI-related stocks.

    The benchmark index, along with the Dow Industrials, are in a correction after falling 10% from their recent highs, and the Nasdaq Composite has erased all of its year-to-date gains.

    Berkshire's smaller decline increased its year-to-date outperformance of the S&P to 12.5 percentage points.

    One Wall Street firm, however, thinks Berkshire's run-up has run its course.

    Argus Research downgraded the B shares to hold from buy Friday, saying the stock is "fully valued" at about 25 times next year's estimate for operating earnings per share.

    As foreshadowed by its 10-Q financial report released almost two weeks ago, Berkshire Hathaway's Q3 13F portfolio snapshot filed with the SEC on Monday showed it wasn't doing much buying and selling of equities this summer.

    And the two largest additions, Lennar and Bending Spoons, had been previously disclosed, along with additional purchases at the start of the fourth quarter.

    The most notable change we didn't expect was a 12% increase in Berkshire's Delta Air Lines position, bringing it just short of a 10% stake, now valued at $5.2 billion.

    Exceeding 10% triggers a number of regulatory burdens, including the requirement to promptly disclose fresh buying or selling, so we may not see additional purchases going forward.

    Delta's return to the portfolio after Warren Buffett sold all of Berkshire's airline stocks in 2020 has been something of a surprise given his bumpy ride with the industry over the years.

    Recent findings suggest that as expected, Berkshire continued to trim its Bank of America stake. After nine consecutive quarters of sales, it's been cut by 56% but remains the fifth largest portfolio holding at $21.4 billion.

    Berkshire also cut another financial, Capital One, by almost 62%, although it was already a relatively small position, now worth $207 million.

    Also notable are two positions that didn't change.

    After adding $17 billion in Q2 to the Alphabet bet that had only been initiated last summer, Berkshire defied some expectations by keeping the holding unchanged.

    Its 106 million shares are valued at $28.1 billion.

    Sources indicate that and for the fourth consecutive quarter, Berkshire's largest equity holding, Apple, didn't change. With a massive boost from the stock's year-to-date gain of 26.1%, the position is now valued at more than $78 billion.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett loves to eat what many would call junk food and drink a lot of sugary beverages. A quarter-century ago, when he was 70, Buffett explained why he still thought a life insurance firm would rate his life expectancy "considerably better than the average.".

    AUDIENCE MEMBER: Every time I hear what you like to eat, Warren, it makes me wonder what your cholesterol level is — (laughter) — or if you even worry about it...

    WARREN BUFFETT: I do know the number, and I don't remember it. My doctor tells me, "It's a little high," but if he states it's a little high, it means it isn't that high, or he would — because he always tries to push me into making a few changes in my life.

    It has been revealed that but he — I've got a wonderful doctor. And I was lucky last year, because I hadn't been in to see him for about five years. And — (laughter) — due to — those guys cost a lot of money, I mean. (Laughter).

    Industry observers note that and due to purely an accident, a reaction to some other medicine I was given when I was out of the city, he got a hold of me, and then he shamed me into having a physical. And it was extremely lucky, because I had a polyp in the colon that would have probably caused trouble, you know, within a couple of years.

    I would say that if you ask my doctor, he would want me to make a few changes, but he would also say that my life expectancy is probably a lot better than the average person of 70.

    Sources indicate that you know, I have no stress whatsoever. Zero. You know, I mean, I get to do what I love to do every day. You know, and I'm surrounded by people that are terrific.

    So that problem in life just doesn't exist for me. You know, and I don't smoke or drink or, well, we'll end it right there. (Laughter).

    Industry observers note that and so, you know, if you were an underwriter for a life tech giant, you would rate me considerably better than the average. You'd rate Charlie better than average, too.

    And I'm sure that, you know, I could change it slightly, perhaps, on the probabilities, you know, if I change my diet dramatically or something. But it's very unlikely to happen.

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,210,976,168,580.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that berkshire's top holdings of disclosed publicly traded stocks in the U.S. and Japan, by market value, based on the latest closing prices.

    Holdings are as of September 30, 2026, as reported in Berkshire Hathaway's 13F filing on November 16, 2026, except for:.

    Also, Buffett's annual letters to shareholders are highly recommended reading. There are collected here on Berkshire's website.

    -- Alex Crippen, Editor, Warren Buffett Watch.

    #85022. Breaking: State and federal battle over prediction markets regulation heats up after midterms

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (943 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: State and federal battle over prediction markets regulation heats up after midterms

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (943 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The turf war between states and the federal government is intensifying after Democrats secured control of Congress and key governorships on midterm elections night.
    • While it was widely expected Democrats would step up oversight of the emerging, multibillion-dollar industry if they won control of Congress, the actions after the elections have come from primarily Republican-led states.
    • Sources indicate that at the same time, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator for prediction markets —  has ramped up its oversight of "mention" markets, where traders speculate on what individuals will say during a speech or broadcast.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The turf war between states and the federal government is intensifying after Democrats secured control of Congress and key governorships on midterm elections night.

    While it was widely expected Democrats would step up oversight of the emerging, multibillion-dollar industry if they won control of Congress, the actions after the elections have come from primarily Republican-led states.

    Sources indicate that at the same time, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator for prediction markets —  has ramped up its oversight of "mention" markets, where traders speculate on what individuals will say during a speech or broadcast. It's a type of event contract the agency has stated is susceptible to manipulation.

    CNBC first reported on Tuesday that the CFTC placed a hold on the certification of markets related to President Donald Trump's words in mid-November. Kalshi remarked it was complying with the order, but CEO Tarek Mansour said at an Axios event on Tuesday that the company disagreed with the regulatory decision.

    In a recent development, on Thursday, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that would ban CFTC-registered entities from listing contracts involving terrorism, assassination, war or military operations. The measure also bars contracts that are "reasonably expected" to resolve based on an individual's death.

    Recent findings suggest that utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed 14 criminal charges against Kalshi and its founders, Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara, on Oct. 28, asserting the tech giant violated a state law that prohibits gambling.

    Kalshi's founders are expected to appear in person at Utah's Third District Court on Dec. 4, according to court documents.

    It has been revealed that "This is a crazy overreach; Utah is clearly playing politics. We look forward to putting a stop to this in court, just like we did in Arizona," said Kalshi's spokesperson Dani Lever.

    Industry observers note that in a separate, civil complaint on Oct. 20, Utah also named institutional market maker Susquehanna International Group as a defendant, along with Kalshi.

    Though Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes filed a criminal complaint against Kalshi in March, a federal judge blocked the case from proceeding in April.

    Recent findings suggest that louisiana's Republican attorney general also filed a complaint to ban multiple exchanges from operating in the state on Nov. 12. A state judge ordered a temporary restraining order against the prediction market companies that same day.

    "Who would have thought that these red states, that were reluctant to jump into the litigation arena, ended up having the most boldest and most innovative solutions," said gambling attorney Daniel Wallach, noting that Louisiana and Utah's latest lawsuits were led by Republican attorneys general.

    Sources indicate that in response, the CFTC sued Louisiana on Nov. 13. Separately, the federal agency filed suit against Arkansas after that state pursued civil enforcement against Kalshi.

    The CFTC has sued 12 states as it tries to defend what it views as its exclusive jurisdiction to regulate prediction markets.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, the CFTC may soon add commissioners. President Donald Trump sent bipartisan nominations to the U.S. Senate on Nov. 12 to fill two of the four open seats on the commission. Chairman Michael Selig has been the only member since his nomination was approved by the Senate in December 2025.

    According to recent reports, nathan Anonick, a Republican, and Matthew Rowland, a Democrat, appeared before the Senate Agriculture Committee on Tuesday. Multiple senators questioned them on the matter of prediction markets. Both demurred when asked whether they viewed sports-related event contracts as gambling.

    Recent findings suggest that the CFTC's position faced another setback in a complicated decision by the Fourth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals this week. The court ruled 2-1 that Maryland can enforce its state gambling law against Kalshi, though the judges disagreed on the reasoning.

    "Judges can't agree with each other on why we're wrong," Kalshi spokesperson Elisabeth Diana noted in a statement about the decision. "This splintered decision, including three separate contradictory opinions, demonstrates there is no unified coherent legal argument against prediction markets.".

    Overall, prediction markets have now seen three losses and one win at the circuit court level. It's widely expected the question of whether states or the federal government can regulate sports-related event contracts will be decided by the Supreme Court.

    Kalshi on Nov. 12  ended its advisory relationship with Donald Trump Jr. The prediction platform pointed to his venture capital firm 1789 Capital having a stake in rival platform Polymarket.

    Industry observers note that though 1789 Capital revealed its holding in Polymarket in August, Kalshi and the president's son ended their relationship after Democrats secured a majority in the House and Senate. Democratic lawmakers are expected to probe companies with relationships to the Trump family.

    Nine Democratic senators, led by Adam Schiff, D-California, on Monday sent a letter to the CFTC asking it to reverse a directive to platforms not to geofence their offerings when they receive unfavorable court rulings stopping exchanges from operating in certain states.

    Geofencing involves the use of location technology to block users in certain jurisdictions from participating in events contracts.

    "Your unilateral decision directly conflicts with active court orders, undermines state and tribal law, and must be reversed," the senators wrote.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, Democratic Rep. Ro Khanna, D-California, has called for Congress to ban sports-related prediction markets entirely.

    It has been revealed that "Kalshi, a $40B tech giant, lets 18 year olds bet on sports. They call it a 'prediction market.' It's gambling," he wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. "Investigate and ban sports prediction markets.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of England’s matchday squad for the Nations League decider in Spain, raising questions over his future involvement under Thomas Tuchel.

    The Everton centre back’s omission means that two rivals who were not in the original squad but were added last week, Dan Burn and James Hill, are now seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order.

    There was a clue as to Tuchel’s uncertainty over Branthwaite when, ahead of last Thursday's Croatia game, he revealed concerns over his suitability to England’s way of playing.

    ‘Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,’ stated the head coach.

    Tuchel then selected Burn ahead of him for the 2-1 win, and said: ‘You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a massive voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe, where they followed in a high press and man-to-man.’.

    It had been thought that Branthwaite, 24, could emerge as a starter at left-sided centre back, given his good club form this season. That now feels unlikely, with Burn and Marc Guehi, who is currently injured, preferred by Tuchel.

    Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of the England squad for their clash against Spain.

    James Hill and Dan Burn, who were both added to the England squad last week, appear to have jumped above Branthwaite in the pecking order.

    Industry observers note that branthwaite has made two substitute appearances under the German, totalling 28 minutes. Also left out of the matchday squad for Sunday’s game in Madrid are Josh King and James Garner.

    In a recent development, everton midfielder Garner came off the bench against Croatia at Wembley and thought he had scored his first England goal, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. He now misses the chance to build on that cameo against the world champions.

    For King, 19, the wait for a senior debut continues after his maiden call-up, a reward for an impressive start to the season with Fulham. Tuchel was forced to trim three players from his 26-man travelling squad, with the return to fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence increasing competition for places.

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Recent findings suggest that lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the tech giant's recent earnings call that China is an "crucial" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    Tyler Herro scores 50, officials miss late out-of-bounds call on Joel Embiid in 76ers' 132-129 win over Bucks

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points Saturday, but that wasn't enough for the Milwaukee Bucks to get their second win of the season in a 132-129 defeat to the Philadelphia 76ers.
    • Milwaukee was deprived of an opportunity to take the lead in the closing seconds when officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds.
    • Sources indicate that rookie Brayden Burries hit a corner 3-pointer for the Bucks to cut the Sixers' lead to 130-129.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points Saturday, but that wasn't enough for the Milwaukee Bucks to get their second win of the season in a 132-129 defeat to the Philadelphia 76ers.

    Milwaukee was deprived of an opportunity to take the lead in the closing seconds when officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds.

    Sources indicate that rookie Brayden Burries hit a corner 3-pointer for the Bucks to cut the Sixers' lead to 130-129. After a timeout, LeBron James threw an inbounds pass to Embiid, who attempted to dribble out the clock near the Milwaukee basket. Embiid stepped out of bounds at the baseline with his left foot, but the officials did not call the turnover and Herro was forced to foul.

    The Bucks could not challenge the non-call because they were out of replay challenges.

    Embiid made his two free throws to put Philadelphia ahead by 3, but the Bucks still had 1.5 seconds remaining to try for a tying basket.

    Industry observers note that herro received the inbounds pass from Kyle Kuzma at the top of the arc and took one dribble to break free from VJ Edgecombe. Shooting from the right elbow, Herro's 3-pointer went in. However, the shot left his hand after the buzzer.

    Industry observers note that the eighth-year guard shot 15 for 23 from the floor, including 7 of 13 on 3-pointers. Herro also hit all 11 of his free throws, adding 11 rebounds and seven assists. Burries finished with 26 points off the bench with 8 rebounds and four assists. Kuzma was the third Bucks player to reach double figures, scoring 12 with five boards.

    Herro's previous career-high was 41 points, reached in a December 2022 win over the Houston Rockets while he was with the Miami Heat.

    Recent findings suggest that milwaukee lost its 13th consecutive game to drop to 1-16 on the season, the worst mark in the NBA. The Bucks' only win came nearly a month ago on Oct. 26, a 110-102 victory over the Indiana Pacers. Up next for them is the Toronto Raptors (6-10) at home on Monday.

    Embiid led the Sixers with 26 points, nearly registering a triple-double with 17 rebounds and nine assists. James added 21 points with 6 boards, 6 assists and 3 steals. Seven Philadelphia players scored in double figures, with Anfernee Simons getting 18 off the bench and Tyrese Maxey tallying 17 points.

    Recent findings suggest that the 76ers improved to 14-3 with the win, tying the Los Angeles Lakers for the NBA's top record. Philadelphia has won five consecutive games and next faces the Portland Trail Blazers (10-5) on Monday.

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a big win for the manufacturer and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Recent findings suggest that some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Recent findings suggest that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and said it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the big indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    It has been revealed that "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he said.

    Recent findings suggest that part of the challenge, Niles remarked, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," mentioned JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he stated, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan said. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the firm in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    In a recent development, "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he stated. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    Industry observers note that one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1327 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech outages are fueling a upcoming doomsday economy

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1327 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A spate of high-profile technology outages that grounded planes, halted email access and slowed bank transactions have left many people worried about artificial intelligence-driven cyberattacks and the state of the U.S.
    • According to recent reports, government officials have dismissed rumors and speculation circulating online that there could be a nefarious culprit for the series of malfunctions.
    • In a recent development, in recent days, the Houston resident has purchased propane and lighter fluid for cooking and heating equipment that can be used without electricity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Americans are shopping like there's no tomorrow.

    A spate of high-profile technology outages that grounded planes, halted email access and slowed bank transactions have left many people worried about artificial intelligence-driven cyberattacks and the state of the U.S. energy grid.

    According to recent reports, government officials have dismissed rumors and speculation circulating online that there could be a nefarious culprit for the series of malfunctions. Despite those assurances, consumers like Sabrina Cepeda are readying for a larger-scale technology blackout or other emergency event.

    In a recent development, in recent days, the Houston resident has purchased propane and lighter fluid for cooking and heating equipment that can be used without electricity. The mother of three also replenished her backup stockpiles of non-perishable foods, hygiene products and allergy medicine in the event that her family is homebound for several days.

    "I have a way to keep my family fed, clean, hydrated, warm and safe," remarked Cepeda, 39. "You want to have these things and not need them, rather than need them and not have them.".

    Recent findings suggest that the doomsday economy is catching a bid. Wall Street and retailers are taking note.

    In a recent development, at least half a dozen major technology outages took place in the U.S. between Nov. 12 and Nov. 17. In that time frame, spending at brands specializing in emergency products spiked about 400% compared with the same period a year prior, according to card data analyzed exclusively for CNBC by Consumer Edge.

    In a recent development, at Ready America, which sells products like emergency survival kits, prepackaged water and high-calorie food bars, sales through e-commerce platforms have seen a roughly five-fold increase in recent days. In addition, corporate customers who keep the Vista, California-based company's supplies in their offices in case of emergency have called in to order more.

    Industry observers note that the tech giant has rarely seen this much demand since the Covid pandemic sent Americans into lockdown more than six years ago, said Ready America President Trevyn Reese. As a result, Ready America asked its suppliers to scale up production. The family-owned business has faced a shortage of water purification tablets, and redirected shoppers to alternative offerings like prepackaged water pouches.

    "With everything going on in the news right now, we've seen a large spike of people wanting to get prepared," stated Reese.

    While the string of outages brought power-related concerns to a boiling point, data highlights that worries had been bubbling under the surface for weeks.

    Sources indicate that shoppers began significantly ramping up buying from emergency preparedness brands late last month, according to Consumer Edge. Around that time, Fox News reported that the Pentagon was preparing U.S. military bases to operate for at least 90 days without external support. Exacerbating those fears was the ongoing war with Iran that President Donald Trump signaled could ramp back up.

    Sources indicate that firearm trade group NSSF said that gun sales rose about 8% in October from the same month a year prior. Retailers and gun manufacturers have anecdotally reported that demand has remained elevated into November, which NSSF said can be attributed to a combination of uncertainty tied to the midterm election and the recent outages.

    In a recent development, "If people are investing in firearms and ammunition, they're telling you very directly, with their wallet, what their priority is," noted Mark Oliva, NSSF's managing director of public affairs. "You're literally investing in a product that's going to be able to protect your life and protect the lives of your family.".

    Now, the doomsday talk has begun making its way to Wall Street.

    Recent findings suggest that mizuho told clients on Monday that consumer worries about the outages — coupled with what the bank called "apocalyptic concerns" swirling on social media — drove shoppers to stock up on emergency supplies at Costco. As a result, Mizuho said it expects a key measure of non-fuel sales growth for Costco in November to rise above 10% for the first time since 2022.

    And RBC mentioned so-called doomsday prepping has had a "real impact" on buying behavior around the globe over recent weeks. Still, the Canadian bank reported that the trend has so far boosted sales for only a small basket of items, such as shelf-stable proteins, water purification products and dry-pantry foods.

    Industry observers note that clients of Richard McWhorter, a private wealth advisor at SRM, have been rushing to Costco to buy goods in bulk and splurging for power generators. McWhorter mentioned he's also fielded questions about how to prepare for a situation in which the financial system goes down.

    "I've never seen anything like this in my life," McWhorter remarked. "There's the financial side of what I do, and then there's the psychological side. And the past two weeks have been much more psychological.".

    Metal dealer American Hartford Gold reported an uptick in customer inquiries this week. Tech giant president Max Baecker remarked he heard from some customers that their interest in products like gold — long considered a safe-haven asset during times of turmoil — was driven by newfound concern about being overly reliant on digital financial networks following a glitch at JPMorgan Chase that affected customer transactions for several hours.

    It has been revealed that vice President JD Vance abruptly canceled his appearance at a Upcoming York Times summit on Wednesday to attend meetings about the technology outages. A day prior, Jay Clayton, the U.S. director of national intelligence, told CNBC that the recent outages were not a cyberattack or a coordinated effort by a foreign nation.

    Still, Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., told CNBC on Wednesday that people were "freaked out" by the outages. Warner, who acts as the vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, remarked that the U.S. was "lucky" to have not yet seen a major AI-generated cyberattack or crisis due to AI agents going rogue.

    Investors may begin pushing companies to accelerate their cybersecurity spending out of an abundance of caution around rogue AI agents following the outages, according to Macro Hive CEO Bilal Hafeez. Such a situation would be reminiscent of the antivirus software push seen during the dot-com boom, he said.

    It has been revealed that the Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) has climbed around 3% over the past two weeks, bucking the downtrend seen among AI stocks and the broader technology trade. The Nasdaq Composite on Friday fell into negative territory for 2026, putting the tech-heavy index on track for its first losing year since 2022.

    To be sure, not everyone on social media has bought into the idea that they should be prepping for a doomsday scenario. In satirical videos posted on TikTok, users joked that they were gearing up by placing orders in the Starbucks drive-thru or purchasing significant quantities of alcohol.

    It has been revealed that still, the topic appears to be on the minds of a growing number of Americans. U.S. Google searches for the term "prepping" have more than doubled when comparing the past month with the same period a year prior. On YouTube, queries for videos about "survivalism," a term describing the practice of preparing for emergencies, have soared by more than 5,000% over the same time frame.

    Cepeda, the Houston mom, sees emergency prep efforts as a way to be safe rather than sorry. She's previously tapped into backup food stashes during extreme weather events like Hurricane Harvey in 2017 and Winter Storm Uri in 2021.

    Sources indicate that but this year is the first time that she's felt she needed to be prepared for a potential emergency caused by technology outages, she remarked. Cepeda and her husband have ensured they have enough cash on hand and fuel in their cars if there's a broader hit to the U.S. power grid, she said.

    In a recent development, "We rely so much on technology," Cepeda remarked. "You need to be able to do these things the more traditional, old-fashioned way.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump suggested Saturday that there could be a bright spot in the latest incursion into the FBI computer database.
    • The president confirmed in an interview with Fox News that a system has been breached that houses information used by law enforcement at all levels to share criminal justice information.
    • The hackers accessed the National Criminal Information Center (NCIC), a database that includes FBI fingerprint records, wanted persons, violent felons, missing persons and related information, two people familiar with the matter told MS NOW.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump suggested Saturday that there could be a bright spot in the latest incursion into the FBI computer database.

    The president confirmed in an interview with Fox News that a system has been breached that houses information used by law enforcement at all levels to share criminal justice information.

    The hackers accessed the National Criminal Information Center (NCIC), a database that includes FBI fingerprint records, wanted persons, violent felons, missing persons and related information, two people familiar with the matter told MS NOW. The database is restricted to law enforcement use but not classified and it is unclear what data was extracted.

    CNN had first reported on the suspected hack, citing sources familiar with the problem.

    In a wide-ranging interview on Fox, Trump said there could be upside from the news.

    "Maybe we'll learn about the voter fraud, all the voter fraud that took place," he mentioned. "I always like to put things on a positive spin.".

    This would be the second recent intrusion into the FBI system; the previous one came in September, when a group known as "ShinyHunters" broke into an FBI jobs website. The result compromised data on current and former FBI employees and shut down part of the agency's operations until the issue was resolved.

    Trump mentioned it's possible there could be information gleaned from the latest hack.

    Recent findings suggest that "I wonder who's doing it, because wouldn't it be great to learn about Russia, Russia, Russia?" he stated. "People should hear about it, because it actually put our country in danger, and so maybe we'll learn things that we wouldn't have learned otherwise.".

    The FBI did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment.

    Anthropic’s record IPO collides with tech’s worst week on Wall Street since 2020

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1260 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that startup investor Ben Narasin is so jazzed about Anthropic's blockbuster IPO that he's planning a party later this month at his Silicon Valley home.
    • "This is a celebration of the most material, significant, and mind-blowingly awesome event that has ever happened in venture capital," Narasin, founding partner of Tenacity Venture Capital, told CNBC in an interview, adding that he didn't even invest in the manufacturer.
    • Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and an additional $26 billion from tech giants that bought at the offer price.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that startup investor Ben Narasin is so jazzed about Anthropic's blockbuster IPO that he's planning a party later this month at his Silicon Valley home. Sake, vodka and Krug Champagne will be served. Each attendee will be given two jars of caviar.

    "This is a celebration of the most material, significant, and mind-blowingly awesome event that has ever happened in venture capital," Narasin, founding partner of Tenacity Venture Capital, told CNBC in an interview, adding that he didn't even invest in the manufacturer.

    Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and an additional $26 billion from tech giants that bought at the offer price. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, lifting Anthropic's market cap to $1.8 trillion and providing a much-needed windfall for Silicon Valley's startup ecosystem.

    It was quite the split-screen moment on Wall Street, which spent the week in an AI-driven tailspin. Led by Nvidia's 23% plunge, which marked the stock's sharpest weekly pullback in 18 years, the Nasdaq slid 10% over the past five trading days in its worst week since the early days of Covid in 2020.

    Investors and analysts spent the week debating whether Anthropic will trade alongside AI hardware, as it's reliant on advanced chips, memory and data centers, or whether it will stand alone as the first public pure-play AI developer and a company that's achieved unrivaled growth in less than six years of existence.

    In a recent development, that question will likely persist for some time, but Friday's market action indicated that Wall Street is skeptical of Anthropic's ability to grow into its lofty valuation. At week's end, the Claude creator's $1.6 trillion fully diluted market cap put it behind just six U.S. companies: Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Nvidia, Amazon and SpaceX.

    With the tech market in turmoil due to rising interest rates, raging anti-AI sentiment and Nvidia's C-suite crisis, Anthropic's IPO was part exuberance, part relief for an industry hungry for exits.

    Industry observers note that after venture-backed IPOs yielded $73 billion in proceeds in 2021, the amount raised in the next four years totaled just $39 billion, according to data from University of Florida emeritus professor Jay Ritter. In 2021, 126 technology companies went public, compared with 34 in 2025.

    It has been revealed that meanwhile, the private market has continued to balloon, with companies raising ever-larger sums at sky-high valuations without the pressures of quarterly earnings. Many startups that had hoped to go public early in the decade fell out of favor in the AI boom. They experienced hefty job cuts, down rounds and acquisitions for pennies on the dollar.

    It has been revealed that "There was a time in Silicon Valley not that long ago where the prevailing wisdom was the default path should be avoiding going public for as long as possible," remarked Somesh Dash, a general partner at venture firm IVP. The view was, "it's too long, it's too hard, it's not worth it," he said.

    Anthropic is very young compared to some of those companies, but it was a huge collector of private capital. Investors poured $141 billion into the AI lab as of September, according to Anthropic's prospectus.

    For a few Silicon Valley firms that contributed to those funding rounds, the returns are unlike anything they've ever seen. At the IPO price, Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners each owned about $25 billion worth of Anthropic stock. Bessemer Venture Partners owned a stake worth roughly $10 billion, partner Byron Deeter noted.

    Matt Murphy, a partner at Menlo, told CNBC's David Faber on Thursday that his firm has more than five limited partners "that we delivered over $1 billion of returns to.".

    "At the end of the day, that's really our job, is to get dollars back into foundations and endowments," Murphy mentioned. "There's a lot of pride in being able to do that.".

    Bessemer's Deeter was also jubilant on Thursday, posting on X that, in addition to being "the largest bet in Bessemer's history," the IPO "is a punctuation mark in the history of both humanity and computation.".

    Sources indicate that that's quite a change from a few years earlier, when Anthropic was hardly generating revenue, and success was far from guaranteed. In 2023, Anthropic's Claude 2 was struggling to keep pace with models from Google and OpenAI. In April 2024, investors at Bessemer wrote in a memo that if Anthropic missed its own targets, there was "a good chance that we lose all or part of our money.".

    Guru Chahal at Lightspeed told CNBC that Anthropic was clearly the team taking a more measured approach to AI. The company looked beyond Nvidia's dominant AI chips, choosing to use alternatives from Amazon and Google as well. Anthropic noted it generated $1.72 in revenue per dollar spent on computing power in the third quarter, up from 68 cents a year earlier.

    "It is true that it required lots of capital, but when you dig in and you realize that capital is going toward compute, and this is the team that's positioned to use that compute in the most effective way, then we could connect those dots," Chahal remarked. He added that those metrics demonstrated it was "going to be a very high-quality business.".

    Anthropic isn't the only substantial win for VCs this year.

    Five months before Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, SpaceX hit the market in what, until this week, was by far the largest IPO in history. SpaceX, which Elon Musk founded in 2002, produced outsized returns for firms including Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz.

    It has been revealed that spaceX and Anthropic alone will make 2026 a monster year for the venture industry, easily exceeding any other year in IPO proceeds. And investors in OpenAI hope appetite remains strong for trillion-dollar companies next year, as the ChatGPT maker is looking to 2027 for a potential offering.

    IVP's Dash said that in his AI portfolio, "a lot of companies are starting IPO prep" even if it's only "year four, year five, year six since inception." He hopes to see at least half a dozen companies go public at valuations north of $10 billion each in the second half of 2027.

    The macro picture, however, is ominous.

    Jensen Huang's sudden departure from Nvidia has left the chip giant without a clear leader at a time when the firm already faced heightened concerns about a slowdown in spending. Nvidia is a key investor in Anthropic and OpenAI and a critical supplier and financing partner for the entire AI industry, which is getting hammered across the board.

    According to recent reports, in January, Democrats will take control of the House and Senate after this month's midterm elections, which included the passage of numerous ballot measures that could stymie data center development. Anthropic investor Brad Gerstner predicted after the election that market dynamics would push Anthropic to price toward the lower end of its range.

    Narasin said he wasn't even sure the company would get that far.

    "I was concerned they'd delay," Narasin mentioned.

    That makes the outcome that much more impressive, he said, after Anthropic priced above its expected range and upsized the offering.

    Recent findings suggest that "This will be bedtime stories for years for future VCs," Narasin said. "There was a organization that was created, backed by angels and later venture" that in a few short years "became the single biggest IPO of all history.".

    — CNBC's Ari Levy contributed to this report.

    WATCH: I like owning Anthropic over the long term, notes Gabelli Funds' John Belton.

    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
